Let \(\alpha\) be the unique number in \((3\pi/2,2\pi)\) satisfying
\[
\coth \alpha+\cot \alpha=\frac2\alpha .
\]
I claim
\[
\Lambda=\alpha^4.
\]

The infimum is attained: after normalizing \(\int_{-1}^1 f^2=1\), the boundary conditions and \(\int (f'')^2\) bound give compactness in \(L^2\), and \(\mathcal V\) is closed.

Let \(f\) be a minimizer and put \(\Lambda=k^4\), \(k>0\). Since the zero-mean constraint is linear, the Euler-Lagrange equation has a constant Lagrange multiplier:
\[
f''''=k^4 f+\eta .
\]
The minimizer is even, so on \([0,1]\),
\[
f'(0)=f'''(0)=0,\qquad f(1)=f'(1)=0,\qquad \int_0^1 f(x)\,dx=0.
\]
Solving the ODE gives
\[
f(x)=A\cosh(kx)+B\cos(kx)+a .
\]
The conditions \(f'(1)=0\), \(f(1)=0\), and \(\int_0^1 f=0\) give
\[
A\sinh k=B\sin k,
\]
\[
A\cosh k+B\cos k+a=0,
\]
\[
\frac{A\sinh k+B\sin k}{k}+a=0.
\]
For a nonzero solution, eliminating \(A,B,a\) yields
\[
\cosh k+\sinh k\cot k-\frac{2\sinh k}{k}=0,
\]
equivalently
\[
\coth k+\cot k=\frac2k. \tag{1}
\]

Conversely, if \(k\) satisfies (1), then
\[
f(x)=\cosh(kx)+\frac{\sinh k}{\sin k}\cos(kx)-\frac{2\sinh k}{k}
\]
on \([0,1]\), extended evenly to \([-1,1]\), belongs to \(\mathcal V\), and satisfies
\[
f''''=k^4 f+\text{constant}.
\]
Multiplying by \(f\), using \(\int f=0\), and integrating by parts with the clamped boundary conditions gives
\[
\int_{-1}^1 (f'')^2\,dx=k^4\int_{-1}^1 f^2\,dx.
\]
Thus every admissible critical value is \(k^4\) for a positive root of (1), and every positive root gives that value.

It remains to identify the smallest positive root. Define
\[
q(k)=\coth k+\cot k-\frac2k.
\]
Using the product formulas for \(\sin k\) and \(\sinh k\), logarithmic differentiation gives, for \(0<k<\pi\),
\[
q(k)
=-4k^3\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^4\pi^4-k^4}<0.
\]
So there is no root in \((0,\pi)\). On \((\pi,2\pi)\),
\[
q'(k)=-\operatorname{csch}^2 k-\csc^2 k+\frac{2}{k^2}<0,
\]
because \(\csc^2 k\ge1\) and \(2/k^2<1\). Also
\[
q(k)\to+\infty\quad(k\to\pi^+),\qquad q(k)\to-\infty\quad(k\to2\pi^-),
\]
so there is exactly one root in \((\pi,2\pi)\). Since
\[
q(3\pi/2)=\coth(3\pi/2)-\frac{4}{3\pi}>0,
\]
that root lies in \((3\pi/2,2\pi)\).

Therefore
\[
\boxed{\Lambda=\alpha^4,\quad \coth \alpha+\cot \alpha=\frac2\alpha,\ \alpha\in(3\pi/2,2\pi).}
\]
